plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a scene diagram of an airplane sighting two points on a straight highway below it. A small colored drawing of a jetliner sits at the upper left, nose pointed left, and a teal dashed horizontal line runs to the right from the aircraft to stand for the horizontal at flight altitude. Across the lower part of the figure a solid black horizontal line represents the highway, with two labeled points on it: A toward the middle and B at the far right. Two gray dashed sight lines drop from the airplane to those points, the line to A being the steeper of the pair and the line to B running much shallower because B lies farther off. Arcs drawn at the airplane mark the two angles opening downward from the dashed horizontal, labeled 25 degrees for the shallow line toward B and 49 degrees for the steep line toward A. Sharing a single vertex for both angles of depression turns the two sight lines and the road into a pair of triangles with a common side. The arrangement supports solving for the airplane's slant distance to A and its elevation above the road once the spacing between the two mileposts is supplied.

interactionPlan.concept: Two angles of depression measured from the same point let you build two right triangles sharing a common vertical side (the altitude), so the slant distances and height can be solved with tangent ratios.
elements: jetliner drawing at upper left, nose pointing left
teal dashed horizontal reference line extending right from the airplane (flight-altitude horizontal)
solid black horizontal highway line across the lower part
point A on the highway, labeled, toward the middle
point B on the highway, labeled, at the far right
gray dashed sight line from airplane to A (steeper)
gray dashed sight line from airplane to B (shallower)
angle arc at airplane between horizontal and sight line to B, labeled 25°
angle arc at airplane between horizontal and sight line to A, labeled 49°
vertical dashed altitude line from airplane down to the highway (revealed during solve phases)
right-angle marker where the altitude meets the highway (revealed during solve phases)
labels for altitude h and slant distances (revealed during solve phases)

interactions.label: Airplane altitude
interactions.teaches: Altitude is the shared vertical side of both right triangles — raising or lowering the plane changes both depression angles and both tangent ratios at once, because tan(angle) = altitude / ground distance in each triangle

interactions.label: Distance from A to B
interactions.teaches: Moving B along the road changes only the shallower triangle's ground leg and its 25° depression angle, while the triangle to A is untouched — the single shared altitude is what links the two triangles

interactions.label: Solve step by step
interactions.teaches: The solution strategy unfolds in order: the dashed horizontal defines the angles of depression, dropping a vertical builds two right triangles with a common side, and then tangent ratios yield the slant distances and elevation

demo_steps.title: Read the scene
demo_steps.narration: From the airplane, the sight line to B is shallower (25° depression) because B is farther away; the sight line to nearer point A drops more steeply at 49°.

demo_steps.title: Change the altitude
demo_steps.narration: Drag the altitude slider: the plane rises or sinks while A and B stay fixed, and both depression angles update together — the altitude appears in the tangent ratio of both triangles.

demo_steps.title: Move point B
demo_steps.narration: Drag the A–B distance slider: B slides along the highway, the shallow sight line and the 25° angle change, but the steep triangle to A is unchanged — only the shared altitude connects them.

demo_steps.title: Draw the horizontal
demo_steps.narration: The teal dashed horizontal through the airplane is parallel to the highway, so each angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the corresponding ground point.

demo_steps.title: Form the right triangles
demo_steps.narration: Dropping a vertical from the plane to the highway creates two right triangles that share the altitude as a common leg: tan 49° = h / (distance to A) and tan 25° = h / (distance to B).

demo_steps.title: Reveal the unknowns
demo_steps.narration: With the A–B spacing known, subtracting the two tangent equations eliminates the ground distances and solves for h; the slant distances to A and B then follow.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Both angles of depression share the airplane's vertex and the same vertical altitude, so the two right triangles are linked by one common side — and that shared side is exactly what makes the unknown height solvable.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Airplane drawing at upper left with a teal dashed horizontal line running right from it; solid black highway line low in the frame with A near the middle and B farther right. Two gray dashed sight lines from the plane to A (steep) and B (shallow). At the airplane, two nested angle arcs open downward from the horizontal: the outer/shallow one labeled 25° (to B) and the inner/steeper one labeled 49° (to A). Angle labels must recompute live as the sliders move (depression angle = arctan(altitude / ground distance)). During solve phases, fade in the vertical dashed altitude with a right-angle marker at the road, then equation annotations like tan 49° = h / x_A and tan 25° = h / x_B, and finally numeric values for h and the slant distances. Keep the airplane, sight lines, and arcs updating smoothly under slider drag.

authoredContext:
A pilot is flying over a straight highway. He determines the angles of depression to two mileposts, 2.1 km apart, to be 25° and 49°, as shown in the figure. Find the distance of the plane from point A and the elevation of the plane.

Diagram of a plane flying over a highway. It is to the left and above points A and B on the ground in that order. There is a horizontal line going through the plan parallel to the ground. The angle formed by the horizontal line, the plane, and the line from the plane to point B is 25 degrees. The angle formed by the horizontal line, the plane, and point A is 49 degrees.

discrepancies: In the rendered screenshot the drawing area appears essentially blank (only the control panel is visible), so the airplane, sight lines, ground, and angle labels cannot be confirmed visually even though the code appears to draw them

Source draws the 25° angle with the small arc adjacent to the horizontal and the 49° angle as the larger arc below it; the generated figure reverses the arc sizes (outer arc = 25°/B, inner arc = 49°/A), so the angle labels sit differently in the wedge than the source

The airplane's vertical projection point O and the dashed altitude line are absent in the default (phase 0) view, and the source's clean two-dashed-line look is replaced by extra dynamic labels (OA, OB) gated behind later phases

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: the airplane points nose-left in the generated figure, while the source plane points nose-right
the airplane is a crude polygon/ellipse composite and noticeably smaller and less recognizable than the source's detailed airliner illustration

the source shows only the two dashed sight lines, dashed horizontal, and angle arcs; the generated figure adds triangle fills, a purple altitude leg, and solution text in later phases (acceptable as pedagogy, but it departs from the source's clean look when advanced)

the angle arc radii and label positions differ slightly: in the source the 49° arc clearly spans from the horizontal down to the steep sight line encompassing the 25° arc region, while the generated arcs are two nested arcs whose labels sit close together near the plane
evaluation.notes: The core geometry — plane, dashed horizontal, two sight lines to A and B with 25°/49° depression angles — matches the source well and the sliders plus a 6-step guided demo add real pedagogical value; main weaknesses are the crude, backwards-facing airplane and slightly cramped angle-arc labeling near the plane vertex.
action_items: Flip the airplane to face right (nose toward B) and improve its silhouette so it reads clearly as the source airliner.
Increase the separation between the 25° and 49° arcs/labels at the plane vertex so the two angle labels cannot crowd each other at small viewport sizes.
Move the 'A' and 'B' ground labels slightly further below the highway line to match the source's clearer spacing.

feedback.rationale: Scores are consistently high (4–5, average 4.4) with concept and interactivity at 5/5; the remaining issues — plane orientation, arc label spacing, ground label placement — are minor polish items that don't impede the figure's correctness or usability.
